Hello everyone, today we will discuss issues related to contracting and operating electrical engineering projects in Canada. Given the extensive content, I will divide the presentation into three parts:

The first part will focus on how to secure engineering projects.

The second part will explain project operation methods.

The third part will illustrate with practical case studies.

It’s important to note that while this lecture centers on electrical engineering projects in Canada, the methods and processes discussed are equally applicable to other engineering projects. This makes the content valuable for builders, developers, property owners, engineers, and electromechanical contractors.

Additionally, having lived abroad for over 20 years, my proficiency in Chinese has declined somewhat. Therefore, I may use both Chinese and English during the presentation to ensure smooth delivery and accurate information transmission. I appreciate your understanding. Thank you.

The agenda for this lecture is as follows:

First, we will provide an overview of electrical projects.

Second, we will discuss how to develop the market for electrical engineering projects.

Third, we will explain how to bid for medium to large-scale electrical engineering projects.

Next, we will introduce methods for operating these projects in Canada.

Finally, I will share experiences and lessons learned from past engineering cases.

Next, I will outline the basic situation of an electrical engineering project.

First, we need to clearly define the scope of work for the electrical engineering project. Electrical engineering typically includes power systems, lighting systems, fire alarm systems, and grounding systems. Some projects also involve low-voltage communication systems and security systems, which encompass access control systems, closed-circuit television (CCTV) surveillance systems, and intrusion alarm systems.

Additionally, the Building Automation System (BAS) is a critical component. In North America, BAS is usually implemented by control contractors, whereas in China, it is often handled by electrical contractors. Other specialized low-voltage systems include nurse call systems used in hospitals.

For every electrical engineering project, the execution process consists of distinct phases. Large-scale formal projects typically commence with the feasibility study phase, followed by the design phase. Upon completion of the design, the project proceeds to the bidding phase, where the winning company assumes responsibility for the construction phase. Some major projects also include a commissioning phase, ultimately concluding with the project closeout phase to finalize the entire process.

Electrical engineering projects are primarily categorized into the following types:

Electrical engineering projects are primarily categorized into the following types:

Industrial Projects: Including heavy industries (such as power generation, mining, oil and gas, pulp, etc.) and light industries (such as the semiconductor sector in manufacturing).

Commercial Projects: Covering various types like schools, office buildings, hospitals, warehouses, etc.

Residential Projects: These include single-family homes (Single House), townhouses (Town House), apartments (Apartment), low-rise buildings (Low Rise), and high-rise buildings (High Rise).

Other Projects: Such as special projects that are not clearly classified.

Next, we will introduce the operational process of electrical projects.

Next, we will introduce the operational process of electrical projects.

First, we need to identify opportunities and clarify the project source. After discovering an opportunity, we must evaluate whether we qualify for bidding. Upon winning the bid, the project enters the implementation phase, which includes forming a team, applying for permits, and commencing on-site construction.

After construction is completed, the project undergoes inspection and then moves into the closing phase, ultimately achieving demobilization.

During the execution of engineering projects, as the electrical contractor, we need to coordinate and collaborate with multiple departments.

During the execution of engineering projects, as the electrical contractor, we need to coordinate and collaborate with multiple departments.

The primary stakeholder is the client/owner, who provides the project funding. Next is the engineering team, responsible for reviewing technical drawings, quality control, and resolving on-site technical issues. Notably, in overseas projects, professional engineers hold veto power—they can reject unreasonable payment applications submitted by contractors to the owner, wielding broader authority compared to domestic projects.

Additionally, coordination with regulatory authorities (AHJ, or Authority-Having Jurisdiction) is required, including the BC Safety Authority, municipal departments, and BC Hydro. Simultaneously, collaboration with other specialty contractors—such as mechanical, plumbing, and framing teams—is essential.

The scale of electrical engineering projects varies significantly, with costs ranging from hundreds of yuan to tens of millions or even hundreds of millions of yuan, typically accounting for 10% to 15% of the total project cost. For electrical contractors, it is necessary to distinguish between high-voltage and low-voltage projects, and undertaking high-voltage projects requires corresponding qualifications. For large-scale projects, electrical contractors may also need to manage subcontractors, such as outsourcing low-voltage systems to specialized firms. Finally, coordination with suppliers involves equipment procurement, delivery timeline management, and on-site commissioning of complex electrical systems.

Construction management is crucial to the success of a project. Poor management can lead to delays, cost overruns, and safety hazards. Therefore, in electrical construction projects, it is essential to strictly implement project management and construction management processes.

During construction, it is mandatory to strictly adhere to the design drawings and relevant electrical codes and standards. For specific applications of North American and Canadian electrical codes, you can refer to my special lecture, which provides detailed technical explanations.

Now let’s discuss the market development strategies for electrical projects. The market can be mainly divided into several categories:

Now let’s discuss the market development strategies for electrical projects. The market can be mainly divided into several categories:

The first category is the public sector, such as government agencies. Canada operates under a three-tier government system, and there are also some state-owned enterprises. Canada has a well-known website called Merx.com, which covers various engineering projects in both the United States and Canada. This website aggregates and publishes a large number of project opportunities, allowing users to access and filter relevant engineering opportunities.

To participate in bidding, an annual fee of approximately CAD 200 is required. A decade ago, Merx.com was the most popular bidding platform, with most government projects and large-scale engineering projects being posted there. However, in recent years, multiple similar platforms have emerged, offering abundant engineering bidding opportunities. Users can download tender documents (RFP or RFQ) and submit their proposals.

In British Columbia, the primary platform used is BC Bid, which mainly posts provincial and municipal government projects.

Additionally, we can obtain project information through social networks to participate in bidding.

Next, we will discuss the private sector, which refers to projects outside of government and state-owned enterprises. These projects are also listed on Merx.com.

For electrical contractors, potential clients mainly include the following categories:  
- First, property owners, such as developers and builders;  
- Second, general contractors;  
- And engineers.  

Engineers are considered potential clients because they are involved in projects from the early stages—without their designs, projects cannot proceed. Therefore, building good relationships with engineers is equally important.  

When acquiring a project, several key factors are crucial.  
First, the quotation must be competitive. Second, construction quality and service must meet high standards. Third, the project must be completed on schedule. Fourth, the project should be completed within the budget.  
Lastly, strong communication and coordination skills are needed to effectively collaborate with all departments involved in the project.

When executing projects in Canada, the counterpart places great emphasis on documentation. From bidding documents, QA/QC to final handover files, Western companies handle everything with utmost professionalism. As a Chinese enterprise, we must prioritize these aspects to integrate into the local mainstream market. Tender proposals and various documents must project a professional image, using formal letterhead templates and avoiding handwritten materials. Additionally, standardized document transfer procedures should be established.

During project execution, it is essential to build the company’s credibility and professional image at every stage. The same principle applies to business operations and market expansion: use official company email for client communication and maintain a professional website. Understanding client needs is critical—know both yourself and your counterpart. Western clients think differently from Chinese counterparts. In China, low prices and kickbacks may secure projects, but such methods are largely ineffective in Canada.

In Canada, state-owned enterprises and government project evaluators are all company employees. Compared to China, corruption and bribery are far less common. Even if someone is tempted, the fear of legal consequences deters misconduct. These professionals prioritize smooth project completion, expecting contractors or consultants to avoid complications and ensure timely delivery.

In North America (including the U.S. and Canada), government officials typically accept gifts valued at no more than CAD 25–30. They often decline dining invitations to avoid suspicion. Thus, employing Chinese-style tactics to win projects rarely works here. We must deeply study Western clients’ mindset, adapt our strategies to meet their expectations, and successfully secure projects.

Next, we will discuss how to proceed with project bidding. The bidding process is relatively straightforward. First, you need to download the RFP (Request for Proposal) or RFQ (Request for Qualification/Quotation) documents from the bidding website. Once downloaded, you can begin preparing your proposal.

The RFP includes a Pre-bid Event, commonly found in government projects, which may be an on-site meeting or conference call and can be mandatory or optional. Mandatory participation is required; failure to attend may result in disqualification.

The RFP outlines the project schedule, including start and end dates and key milestones. The scope of work is the most critical component, detailing the specific tasks to be performed. Bidder qualifications are specified, such as required certifications, insurance, bonds, and other compliance requirements. Some projects also require bidders to provide summaries of similar past projects as references.

The document will clearly state the final bid submission deadline and the deadline for submitting questions. For construction projects, safety requirements are particularly important. In federal and provincial government projects, security clearance requirements are often involved.

The proposal requirements typically consist of two parts: the technical proposal and the price proposal. The technical proposal should include team structure, member resumes, project experience, implementation methods, etc. Different projects have specific formatting and page limits for proposals, so bidders must read and adhere to these requirements carefully.

Regarding the Reference Project, we have already discussed it. The Proposal Format has detailed requirements including page limits and section divisions. For example, the Resume is typically limited to two pages.

Regarding the Reference Project, we have already discussed it. The Proposal Format has detailed requirements including page limits and section divisions. For example, the Resume is typically limited to two pages.

In addition to the RFP (Request for Proposal) itself, bidders may raise questions after its release. To address these questions, Addendum documents will be issued. An RFP for a project might include 10 addenda, or just one, or none at all.

These addenda, together with the RFP, form the complete bidding documents and must all be considered during the bidding process as they carry legal weight.

Next, we will discuss the bidding process.

First, upon receiving the RFP/RFQ documents, carefully review them to clarify the project scope and client requirements. If there are any questions, raise them with the client through the specified channels in the documents.

First, upon receiving the RFP/RFQ documents, carefully review them to clarify the project scope and client requirements. If there are any questions, raise them with the client through the specified channels in the documents.

Subsequently, perform a cost estimation based on the project requirements and scope, including both direct and indirect costs.

Next, prepare the bid content and relevant supporting documents, such as various certifications and insurance documents.

Finally, consolidate all materials into a complete bid package, which can be submitted to the client electronically or in hard copy, depending on the project requirements.

Below, we will share some practical tips for the bidding process.

Here are some personal suggestions for your reference.

Here are some personal suggestions for your reference.

Before bidding, evaluate whether the company has experience in similar projects as a reference for the bid. At the same time, prepare a professional bidding template. When providing project quotations, use the Electrical Estimate Book or professional software to estimate the total project cost. The bid document should clearly articulate the understanding of the scope of work and provide detailed explanations on how to handle potential scope changes and related cost adjustments. For example, if a scope change leads to project delays, the bid should explicitly outline the mitigation plan.

Regarding the hourly rate, it is advisable to maintain competitiveness—neither too high nor too low. While a price advantage can help in bidding, excessively low quotes may raise doubts about technical capabilities. Taking federal government projects as an example, evaluation criteria often exclude the highest and lowest bids because overly low quotes are seen as indicators of unreliable technical competence. Therefore, it is recommended to bid 10% to 20% below the normal market level, as this increases the chances of winning the contract.

For companies lacking experience, consulting a professional estimator or project manager is recommended, as they can provide valuable insights.

For companies lacking experience, consulting a professional estimator or project manager is recommended, as they can provide valuable insights.

Additionally, when preparing tender documents, it is essential to hire native English speakers for polishing to ensure linguistic accuracy. At the same time, carefully verify whether the quoted price covers all costs. Notably, project delays are a common occurrence, so it is necessary to consider how to address the resulting cost increases.

In the international engineering sector, contractors often adopt a typical strategy: offering highly competitive prices during the bidding phase and then securing profits through change orders. This phenomenon is particularly prevalent in poorly managed projects.

Furthermore, contractual legal clauses must be given due attention. If in doubt, consulting a professional lawyer is advisable. Our company has extensive experience in executing electrical projects and can provide relevant consultation and assistance, with services billed on an hourly basis.

The above are recommendations on how to participate in bidding for electrical projects.

In the next video, we will explore how to operate electrical engineering projects.
